decompositions.boundaries: Change 1: comma-separated export to JSON Lines (A to B); it hands over a working JSON Lines export that both formats can coexist with. Change 2: retire the comma-separated reader once the outside consumer reads JSON Lines; it can start only after the consumer has adopted JSON Lines, and it hands over a state where only JSON Lines is read. Change 3: remove the transition option that served both formats; it retires what Change 1 introduced and starts only after Change 2 leaves no user of the old path.

explanation.current: Today (A) the export writes a header row id,title,body and one comma-separated line per note (H1), writes every note without dropping any (H2), and for an empty store exits with 0 and writes only the header (H3). All three Cases are green; they prove A only.
explanation.intended: In the intended outcome (B) the export writes one JSON object per line and no header (B1), still writes every note (B2), and for an empty store exits with 0 and writes nothing (B3). B1 is new and needs its own Case; B2 and B3 need Cases that run against the new export.
explanation.changes: The comma-separated format is replaced by JSON Lines. B1 is introduced. The no-drop guarantee and the exit code 0 for an empty store are kept. The header and the empty-store header output are replaced by no header and empty output.
explanation.superseded_and_protected: Superseded (historical): H1, the header row and comma-separated lines, and the 'writes only the header' part of H3; these are recorded as superseded and must not be kept as protections of B or cited as proof of B. Protected (enduring): H2/B2, that no note is dropped, and the exit code 0 for an empty store from H3/B3. Their Cases stay and are re-run against the new export. Dropping the no-drop Case would retire a protection B still needs. H3 is mixed and is split into an enduring exit code and a historical header output.
explanation.evidence: B's own green Cases (B1 to B3) show that B holds, not that the step was taken. Transition evidence belongs to the Change record: the header Case recorded as superseded, and the enduring Cases (no note dropped, exit code 0 on an empty store) kept and green against the new export, for example the same set of notes from both exports on the same store. Unknown: whether the consumers of the old format exist outside the notes tool.

observerVerdict.boundaryReasoning: Best on D2: for each Change it says what it hands over (a working JSON Lines export, then a state where only JSON Lines is read), why order matters (consumer adoption, then no remaining user of the old path), and that Change 3 retires what Change 1 introduced, with no internal plan. D1 is still left as one Change with no justification.
doubtfulLabels: S7 labelled transition/none: it also asserts the same set of notes, which is an enduring claim, so it should be mixed
evidence is weaker: no case that fails on the old export and passes on the new, only 'the Change record' and 'same set of notes'
